correctness.rationale: For one r-set the probability is its internal class probability times q^{r(n-r)}, q=1-p. Distinct sizes rule out any shared vertex in the mixed product. A disjoint pair has independent internal events and the sum of the two separate absent-edge counts minus rs, because the cross edges are counted twice. There are binom(n,r)binom(n-r,s) ordered disjoint pairs; dividing by the positive means gives R q^{-rs}. This is strictly increasing from R<1 to infinity, while r+s>n gives a zero mixed moment and strictly negative covariance. The inverse of R telescopes as the product of (n-i-j)/(n-i-j-1) over 0≤i<r, 0≤j<s. Every factor is at least n/(n-1) and at least one is larger. The logarithmic mean of the same factors is 1/n+(r+s-1)/(2n²)+O(n^-3), yielding the stated threshold expansion on exponentiating. The sample n=6, (r,s)=(1,2) gives R=2/3.
